children: TOKYO--Japan's exports rose for a 14th straight month in October, lifted by demand for goods related to artificial intelligence and signaling resilience that backs the case for more interest-rate increases.

Shipments climbed 20.5% from a year earlier, following September's 16.5% increase, government data showed Wednesday. Demand for electronic components, chip-making machines and cars contributed to the growth.
That was slightly higher than the 20.0% rise expected in a poll of economists by data provider LSEG.
Solid external demand is a welcome bright spot for Japan after government data earlier this week showed sluggish private consumption stalled overall economic growth.

While persistent inflation continues to weigh on consumer sentiment, expectations are building that the Bank of Japan will raise interest rates as soon as December. As officials assess the broader impact of monetary tightening, a resilient export performance offers a vital buffer to support growth.
Markets are pricing in an 85% chance of a rate increase at the central bank's policy meeting set for next month.
